subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: An Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner (APFC) functions primarily as:

options.option_text: A quasi-judicial authority under Section 7A of EPF Act
A civil judge of the first class

explanation: I.1 APFC Role — APFC is the primary quasi-judicial officer under Section 7A who determines dues. He is NOT a civil judge, though he has some civil-court powers under Section 7A(2).

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: APFC is recruited as a Group 'A' Gazetted officer in which pay level?
explanation: I.1 APFC Role — APFC is recruited at Pay Matrix Level 10 (₹56,100 entry pay), Group A Gazetted.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Which of the following is NOT a core function of an APFC?
explanation: I.1 APFC Role — Monetary policy is framed by RBI, not EPFO. All other functions are core APFC duties.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: The UPSC EPFO APFC 2025 Recruitment Test (held 30 Nov 2025) consisted of:
explanation: I.2 Exam Pattern — Recruitment Test for APFC = 120 MCQs, 2 hours, 300 marks. Negative marking 1/3rd.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Negative marking in UPSC EPFO APFC Recruitment Test is:
explanation: I.2 Exam Pattern — UPSC RT prescribes 1/3rd negative marking for each wrong answer.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: UPSC Advt. 52/2025 (July 2025) notified how many APFC vacancies?
explanation: I.2 Exam Pattern — Special Advt 52/2025 notified 74 APFC + 156 EO/AO = 230 posts total.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Which of the following is NOT in the published UPSC EPFO APFC syllabus?
explanation: I.3 Syllabus — Quantum field theory is NOT part of the syllabus. All other three are syllabus topics.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: 'Industrial Relations and Labour Laws' as a syllabus topic primarily tests:

options.option_text: Indian labour legislation and welfare Acts
British common law on master & servant

explanation: I.3 Syllabus — Syllabus covers Indian labour laws: ID Act, Minimum Wages, Bonus, Gratuity, SS Code etc.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Which domain carries the LARGEST weightage in APFC syllabus?
explanation: I.3 Syllabus — Social Security and Labour laws directly relate to APFC's job — highest weightage.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Which section of EPF Act empowers an officer to conduct a quasi-judicial enquiry to determine dues?
explanation: I.1 APFC Role — Section 7A enables a quasi-judicial enquiry for determination of dues. 7B is review; 7Q is interest.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: The authority appointing an APFC under EPF Act is:
explanation: I.1 APFC Role — Under S.5D, the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) appoints APFC, RPFC and other officers after Central Govt approval of creation of posts.

subject: APFC Role & Exam
stem: Minimum educational qualification prescribed for APFC (UPSC notification 2025) is:

options.option_text: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university

explanation: I.3 Syllabus — Bachelor's from a recognised university is the minimum qualification.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The Employees' Provident Fund & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies to every factory or establishment employing:
explanation: II.4 Applicability — S.1(3)(a): EPF Act applies to every establishment employing 20 or more persons. Central Govt may extend to establishments with <20 by notification in Official Gazette.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following establishments can be brought under EPF Act by notification even if they employ fewer than 20 persons?

options.option_text: Shops under Shops & Establishments Act only

explanation: II.4 Applicability — S.1(3)(b) empowers Central Govt to notify any establishment for coverage with at least 2 months' prior notice in the Official Gazette.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A factory once covered under EPF Act ceases to be covered when the employee strength falls below 20. True or False?

options.option_text: True only if fall persists for 12 months
True only with Central Govt approval

explanation: II.4 Applicability — S.1(5): 'An establishment to which this Act applies shall continue to be governed by this Act notwithstanding that the number of persons employed therein at any time falls below 20.'

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The EPF Act does NOT apply to:

options.option_text: Co-operative societies employing less than 50 persons and working without power

explanation: II.4 Applicability — Co-operatives with <50 workers operating without the aid of power are specifically excluded under S.16(1)(a). They can, however, opt to join voluntarily.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage of a new joiner is currently:
explanation: II.4 Applicability — Wage ceiling was raised from ₹6,500 to ₹15,000 w.e.f. 1 September 2014. An employee earning >₹15,000 at joining can still opt in jointly with employer.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: 'Basic wages' under S.2(b) of EPF Act excludes which of the following?
explanation: II.4 Definitions — S.2(b) excludes DA, HRA, overtime, bonus, commission, presents from employer from basic wages definition — though DA IS added for contribution computation under S.6.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: In Bridge & Roof Co. vs Union of India (1963), the Supreme Court held that for inclusion in basic wages, an allowance must be:

options.option_text: Universally, necessarily and ordinarily paid to all workmen

explanation: II.4 Definitions — Bridge & Roof (1963) laid the 'universally, ordinarily and necessarily paid' test for identifying basic wages, later reaffirmed in Surya Roshni (2019).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: In Surya Roshni Ltd vs EPFO (28 Feb 2019), the Supreme Court held:

options.option_text: Variable allowances paid to all workers are part of basic wages
Piece-rated wages are excluded from EPF

explanation: II.4 Definitions — Surya Roshni held that special allowances which are universally paid to all employees are 'basic wages' and hence attract PF contribution. Burden of proof on the employer.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The rate of employee's contribution to EPF (standard rate) is:

options.option_text: 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance

explanation: II.5 Contributions — S.6: Employee contributes 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance. Employer matches 12%.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Out of the employer's 12% contribution, what percentage is diverted to EPS 1995?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Employer's 12% is split: 8.33% → EPS (capped at ₹1,250 on ₹15,000 wage); 3.67% → EPF. If wages exceed ₹15,000, entire EPS share goes if higher-pension option exercised.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: For certain notified establishments the contribution rate is reduced from 12% to:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — 10% rate applies under S.6 proviso to: establishments with <20 employees declared as sick, those in five specified industries (jute, beedi, brick, coir, guar gum), and certain others.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Government of India's contribution to EPS 1995 is:

options.option_text: 1.16% of wages up to the wage ceiling

explanation: II.5 Contributions — The Central Government contributes 1.16% of wages (capped at ₹15,000) to EPS, making the total EPS contribution equal to 8.33% + 1.16% = 9.49% of capped wages.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The administrative charges paid by the employer to EPF (since 1-Jun-2018) are:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — EPF admin charges have been 0.5% of EPF wages since 1 June 2018 (minimum ₹500/month, or ₹75 for non-functional establishments). Earlier 1.10%, then 0.65%.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The EDLI administrative charges payable by employer are:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — EDLI admin charges are 0.01% (minimum ₹200/month) since April 2017.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: EPF interest rate declared for FY 2025-26 (239th CBT) is:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — 239th CBT retained 8.25% for FY 2025-26 — third consecutive year. Needs MoF concurrence; credited June-Aug 2026.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which body recommends the EPF interest rate annually?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — CBT is the supreme policy body under S.5A. It recommends; MoF concurs; then credited.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The interest on EPF accumulations is credited:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Interest is declared annually by CBT, approved by MoF, and credited retrospectively to each member's account for the relevant financial year.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A member's EPF account becomes INOPERATIVE (no further interest credit) after:

options.option_text: 3 years of cessation with no claim
36 months from cessation — earlier rule, now withdrawn

explanation: II.5 Contributions — Since 2016, interest is credited on inoperative accounts too, till member attains 58 years of age, reversing the earlier '36-month stop' rule.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) is constituted under which section of EPF Act?
explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — S.5A constitutes CBT as a tripartite body — Central Govt + State Govts + employers + employees.

subject: EPF Act 1952

options.option_text: Union Labour Minister (nominated by Central Govt)

explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — Union Minister of Labour & Employment is the ex-officio Chairman of CBT.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: CPFC (Central Provident Fund Commissioner) functions as:
explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — CPFC is the Member-Secretary of CBT and Chief Executive of EPFO. He implements CBT decisions.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Default in payment of employee's EPF contribution deducted from wages is punishable under:
explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14(1A): Default in deducted contributions = imprisonment 1-3 years (min 1 year) + fine ₹10,000 mandatory. Higher punishment than default in employer's own share.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Under S.14(1) of EPF Act, making a false statement or representation attracts:

options.option_text: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹5,000 or both
Imprisonment up to 3 years without fine

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14(1): false statement = up to 1 year jail or fine up to ₹5,000 or both.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Section 14B of EPF Act empowers the authority to levy:

options.option_text: Damages for delayed payment of contributions

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14B authorises levy of damages for default in payment, separate from interest under S.7Q.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Post 15 June 2024, damages under S.14B / Para 32A are levied at:

options.option_text: Uniform 1% per month (12% per annum) with no cap

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — Amendment dated 14 June 2024 (effective 15 June 2024) made damages a uniform 1% per month (12% p.a.) with no upper cap, replacing the older slab-rate (17-37% max).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Interest payable under Section 7Q of EPF Act for delayed deposit of contribution is:
explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.7Q prescribes simple interest at 12% per annum from due date till date of actual payment. This is independent of S.14B damages.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following is TRUE about S.7Q interest?

options.option_text: It requires a separate quasi-judicial order
It is automatic and payable on default
It is chargeable only if delay exceeds 60 days

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.7Q interest is automatic and does not require a show-cause notice — pure arithmetical charge. Unlike S.14B damages, no discretion or enquiry is required.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Repeat offences under EPF Act (S.14AA) are punishable with:
explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14AA: enhanced imprisonment of not less than 2 years but may extend to 5 years + fine not less than ₹25,000 for repeat offences.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A Section 7A enquiry is conducted by an officer of which rank or higher?
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A empowers Central PF Commissioner and officers notified — APFC and above are authorised. EO/AO cannot conduct 7A enquiries.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following civil-court powers is available to a S.7A officer?

options.option_text: Issuing commissions for examination of witnesses

explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A(2) vests powers of civil court under CPC for: (a) enforcing attendance, (b) requiring document production, (c) issuing commissions, (d) receiving evidence on affidavit.

subject: EPF Act 1952
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — The order must be a speaking order, giving reasons (principles of natural justice). This principle flows from Articles 14/21 & S.7A(2) civil-court powers.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Review of a S.7A order can be sought under:
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7B allows review of 7A orders on grounds like error apparent on the face of the record, discovery of new evidence, etc. Appeal lies to CGIT under S.7I.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Appeal from a S.7A order lies to:
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7I: appeal lies to the Central Government Industrial Tribunal (also called EPFAT). Pre-deposit of 75% of determined dues required under S.7O.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Pre-deposit requirement for an appeal to CGIT under S.7O is:
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7O requires 75% pre-deposit of determined amount (Tribunal may waive/reduce for hardship).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Inspector powers under EPF Act flow from:
explanation: II.9 Inspector Powers — S.13 empowers appointment of Inspectors and prescribes their powers — search, examination, calling for records etc.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following is NOT an Inspector's power under S.13?

options.option_text: Require production of books of account

explanation: II.9 Inspector Powers — Seizure by inspector is subject to limits; records must be examined and copies taken — indefinite retention without cause is not permitted.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Obstruction of an Inspector under S.13 is an offence punishable under:

options.option_text: S.14(2) — imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹4,000

explanation: II.9 Inspector Powers — S.14(2) makes obstruction of or failure to comply with Inspector's requisition punishable.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Under S.12 of EPF Act, an employer:

options.option_text: Can recover employee contribution from wages without restriction
Cannot reduce wages of an employee merely because of liability under the Act
Is always liable for interest on delay

explanation: II.9 Inspector Powers — S.12 prohibits reduction of wages (or any compensation) by the employer merely to counter his EPF contribution liability — protects employees from indirect pass-through.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which paragraph of EPF Scheme 1952 governs damages?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Para 32A (amended 14 Jun 2024) lays down the uniform 1% per month damages structure.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which paragraph governs voluntary withdrawal from EPF?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Para 72 of EPF Scheme governs settlement of accounts on retirement, death, or after 2 months unemployment.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: An EPF member below 58 years can make NON-refundable withdrawal for which of the following?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Para 68-B, 68-K, etc. permit partial NON-refundable withdrawals for housing, marriage, education, medical treatment, and some other specified contingencies.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A member can withdraw entire EPF balance if continuously unemployed for:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Para 69 (pre-Oct 2025 rule): after 2 months → 100% withdrawable. Post 13-Oct-2025 CBT: 75% immediate; remaining 25% only after 12 months continuous unemployment. After 1 month: 75% advance (post-Covid rule).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The wage ceiling for EDLI and EPS mandatory coverage is:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Both EPS and EDLI use the ₹15,000 wage ceiling. EDLI's insurance benefit also uses capped wage.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which category of workers was universally added to EPF coverage by Code-period amendments?

options.option_text: Gig and platform workers (under SS Code)

explanation: II.5 Contributions — SS Code 2020 expanded social security coverage to gig and platform workers — administered through a new Social Security Fund.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Once a member crosses age 58, what happens to EPS contribution?

options.option_text: Stops; entire 12% of employer goes to EPF
Goes to pension fund as before

explanation: II.5 Contributions — On attaining age 58, EPS contribution stops. Thereafter, the full 12% employer share goes to EPF. Monthly pension starts (subject to eligibility).

subject: EPF Act 1952
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Interest is credited annually but calculated on the running monthly balance (so effectively compounded yearly).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Limitation for initiating a S.7A enquiry is:

options.option_text: No express limitation under EPF Act

explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — No express period of limitation for S.7A. However, courts have held delay must be explained (doctrine of reasonableness). Post Vivekananda (SC 2019), EPFO issued 14-Feb-2020 guidelines curbing 'roving' 7A notices.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following orders is made by the 7A officer after hearing?
explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A is specifically to determine the amount due from an employer (arrears of contribution, interest, damages sometimes clubbed in same proceedings via composite SCN).

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Recovery of EPF dues under Section 8 is NOT made through which of the following modes?

options.option_text: Attachment of movable property by RBI

explanation: II.9 Recovery — Modes under S.8B-8G include attachment, sale, arrest, receiver — all on certificate issued by RPFC acting as recovery officer. RBI does not attach movables for EPFO.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Recovery certificate under EPF Act is issued by:
explanation: II.9 Recovery — Authorised Officer (usually RPFC/APFC) issues certificate under S.8B. Recovery officer then executes through modes in S.8E.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Excluded employee under Para 2(f) of EPF Scheme is one who:

options.option_text: Works less than 180 days a year

explanation: II.4 Applicability — Para 2(f): member who has attained 58 and drawn full EPF amount is 'excluded employee'. Also: those above ₹15,000 wage at joining who don't opt in.

subject: EPF Act 1952

options.option_text: Whole of India including J&K; (post Aug 2019)

explanation: II.4 Applicability — Original S.1(2) excluded J&K.; Post abrogation of Art. 370 (Aug 2019), EPF Act extended to UT of J&K; and Ladakh from 31-Oct-2019.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Maximum number of employers' representatives on CBT (S.5A) is:
explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — S.5A(1)(d): maximum 10 employer representatives + 10 employee representatives (parallel 5A(1)(e)). Central Govt reps capped at 5; State Govt reps at 15.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Executive Committee of CBT is constituted under:
explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — S.5AA empowers CBT to constitute an Executive Committee; day-to-day work is supervised by EC.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A Regional Committee (RC) is constituted under:
explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — S.5B constitutes Regional Committees for advising CBT on regional matters. Usually one per State/UT.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Offences by a company are dealt with under:

options.option_text: S.14A — every person in charge shall be liable

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14A: every person in charge of and responsible for the conduct of business is deemed guilty, unless proved that offence occurred without knowledge or due diligence exercised.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which RCM code applies to EPF establishment registration online?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — ECR 2.0 (launched 2017) is the unified electronic challan-return system used by employers for monthly EPF returns.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY), Govt subsidised:

options.option_text: Employer's entire 12% for new employees earning < ₹15,000 for 3 years (ended Mar 2019)

explanation: II.5 Contributions — PMRPY (2016-19): Govt paid 12% employer EPS+EPF contribution for new employees earning <₹15,000 — scheme ceased for new registrations after 31 March 2019.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: ABRY (Atmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana), Oct 2020-Mar 2022, subsidised:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — ABRY subsidised the full 24% (both shares) for establishments up to 1,000 employees, and only employee share for larger establishments — payable for 24 months.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Which of the following is NOT specifically listed in Schedule I of EPF Act?
explanation: II.4 Applicability — Schedule I lists specific industries that attract EPF coverage. Video editing is NOT listed; such establishments come under general S.1(3)(b) notification.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: EPFO's current operational jurisdiction is across how many Regional Offices?
explanation: II.4 Applicability — EPFO operates through 122 Regional Offices (as of 2025) — reduced/rationalised from earlier 135+ through reorganisation.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The Centralised Pension Payment System (CPPS) went live nation-wide on:
explanation: II.4 Applicability — CPPS went live across all 122 ROs on 1 January 2025; benefits ~70 lakh EPS pensioners by enabling bank-account-agnostic pension disbursal.

subject: EPF Act 1952

options.option_text: EPF interest rate 8.25% for FY 25-26 + PF Amnesty Scheme

explanation: II.6 CBT Structure — 239th CBT (Feb-Mar 2026): retained EPF rate 8.25% + announced PF Amnesty Scheme for voluntary compliance and reduced damages.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Universal Account Number (UAN) is unique to:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — UAN is a unique 12-digit number assigned to each EPF member; it is portable across jobs, linking multiple Member IDs.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: A member can e-transfer (auto-transfer) EPF balance on job change using:

options.option_text: Form 13 — online via UAN with KYC update

explanation: II.5 Contributions — Online Form 13 via EPFO member portal allows auto-transfer of EPF accumulation on job change, subject to Aadhaar-linked UAN + employer KYC.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: The auto-settlement ceiling for EPF advance claims was raised (2024-25) to:
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Auto-settlement ceiling raised to ₹5 lakh w.e.f. 24-Jun-2025 (earlier ₹1 lakh from Nov-2024) — used for medical/education/housing advance claims processed in ~3 days.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Failure to pay EPS contribution is punishable under:

options.option_text: S.14(1B) — imprisonment up to 1 year + fine up to ₹5,000

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14(1B): default in EPS contribution = imprisonment up to 1 year + fine. Note: 14(1A) is specifically for deducted-but-not-deposited EPF, higher punishment.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Under amended Para 32A, damages are chargeable from:
explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — Damages accrue from the due date of contribution (15th of next month, prior to 2016; 15th of the relevant month after 2016 amendment) till date of actual deposit.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Bombay HC (Kiran Rajaram Jadhav vs EPFO, 2026) held:

options.option_text: Employees can be denied higher pension if employer records missing
Missing employer records alone cannot be a ground to deny higher pension
EPF dues can never be recovered

explanation: II.8 7A Enquiry — Bombay HC directed EPFO to re-examine applications rejected solely on the ground of missing employer documents — employees cannot suffer for employer's negligence.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Interest rate history: which year saw the LOWEST EPF rate in the last decade?
explanation: II.5 Contributions — FY 2021-22 rate was 8.10% — the lowest in four decades. FY 22-23 it rose to 8.15%, then 8.25% since FY 23-24.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: S.11 of EPF Act deals with:

options.option_text: Priority of payment in case of insolvency/winding-up

explanation: II.9 Recovery — S.11: EPF dues have priority over other debts (except secured creditors) in insolvency. Post IBC 2016, status modified — EPF dues are excluded from liquidation estate.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Under S.9 of EPF Act, EPF accumulations are:
explanation: II.9 Recovery — S.9: PF accumulations are not liable to attachment under decree/order of any court — full protection until paid out.

subject: EPF Act 1952
explanation: II.5 Contributions — Employer pays 0.5% EDLI on capped wages of ₹15,000, i.e., maximum ₹75 per employee per month. No employee contribution to EDLI.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Establishments that wish to run a private PF trust must get exemption under:
explanation: II.4 Applicability — S.17 grants exemption to an establishment running a private PF trust, provided employee benefits are not less favourable than statutory EPF. Para 27/27AA gives interim relaxation.

subject: EPF Act 1952
stem: Cognisance of offences under EPF Act is taken only by:

options.option_text: Magistrate of the first class or above, on complaint by EPFO

explanation: II.7 Offences & Penalties — Offences are cognisable only on a complaint by authorised officer; triable by Metropolitan/JMFC.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: The Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) 1995 came into force on:
explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — EPS 1995 was notified on 16 November 1995 (retrospectively from that date) — replaced Family Pension Scheme 1971.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: EPS 1995 is mandatory for employees whose monthly wages at the time of joining are:
explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — EPS applicability is governed by the wage ceiling of ₹15,000 at time of joining (raised from ₹6,500 on 1 Sep 2014). Above ₹15,000, employee may opt in with employer.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Government of India contributes to EPS at:
explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — GoI contributes 1.16% on capped wages (₹15,000), making total EPS inflow 9.49% (of which 8.33% from employer + 1.16% from GoI).

subject: EPS 1995
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Monthly Pension = (Pensionable Salary × Pensionable Service) ÷ 70.

subject: EPS 1995
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Para 11(3) w.e.f. Sep 2014: average of last 60 months' wages (earlier last 12 months). Capped at ₹15,000 unless higher pension option.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Minimum service for EPS monthly pension is:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Para 9: Minimum 10 years of pensionable service required for monthly pension. <10 years = withdrawal benefit under Table D.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: If an employee's pensionable service is 25 years + pensionable salary ₹15,000, his monthly pension will be:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — (15,000 × 25) / 70 = ₹5,357 per month.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Bonus years added for pensionable service if actual service ≥ 20 years:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Para 10(2): 2 bonus years added to pensionable service if member has 20+ years of service.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Minimum monthly pension under EPS (notified Sept 2014) is:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Minimum pension of ₹1,000/month was introduced w.e.f. 1 Sep 2014. Proposal to raise to ₹7,500 (2024-26) is pending — NOT yet notified.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Superannuation pension is payable on attaining age:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Para 12: Superannuation pension at age 58 (normal retirement age under EPS).

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Early pension (reduced) can be taken from age:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Para 12(7): Early pension from age 50 — with reduction of 4% per year short of 58 (so 50 yr old gets ~68% of full).

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Widow/widower pension is what % of member's pension?
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Widow pension = 50% of member's pension or minimum ₹1,000, whichever higher. Payable for life.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Each child pension (maximum 2) is what % of member's pension?
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Children pension = 25% of widow pension, for max 2 children, till age 25 or till marriage.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Orphan pension (no surviving parent) is at:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Orphan pension = 75% of widow pension or ₹750 whichever higher — for max 2 orphans.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: If a member dies before qualifying service of 10 years, his family gets:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Even if deceased had <10 years, family gets widow pension (minimum service treated as 10 yrs) plus withdrawal benefit is not given — death-in-service relaxation under Para 12.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Disability pension under EPS is payable:

options.option_text: If member becomes permanently totally disabled even if <10 years service

explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Para 15: Permanent total disablement pension is payable irrespective of the length of service — relaxation of 10-year minimum.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Withdrawal benefit under Table D is computed in:

options.option_text: Both A and B, depending on date of leaving service
Only flat rate irrespective of service

explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Earlier Table D was in years; amendment dated 14 Jun 2024 made it month-wise for fairness to members with <10 years service. Both apply depending on leaving date.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: R.C. Gupta vs RPFC (Oct 2016, SC) held:

options.option_text: Higher pension option cannot be exercised
Members who contributed on actual wages (>₹15k) can opt for higher pension

explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — R.C. Gupta recognised the right to contribute on actual salary for higher pension — precursor to Sunil Kumar.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Sunil Kumar vs EPFO (4 Nov 2022, SC) order:

options.option_text: Extended higher pension eligibility to all pre-Sep 2014 members who contributed on actual wages

explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — Sunil Kumar: members who were in service as on 1 Sep 2014 AND had contributed on actual wages above ceiling are entitled to higher pension — joint option with employer.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Deadline for exercising higher pension option (after extensions) was:
explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — Deadline extended multiple times by SC directions → finally 11 July 2023.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Status of higher-pension applications processing (as per PIB Nov 2025):
explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — PIB release Nov 2025: ~99% of higher-pension applications processed; PPOs issued to 1,24,457+ pensioners; ~12,572 in final stages.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: The EPS corpus is maintained under:
explanation: III.15 Funds & CPPS — Pension Fund is a separate fund under S.6A and Para 4 of EPS. Its investments are governed by pattern prescribed by Central Govt.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: CPPS (Centralised Pension Payment System) was rolled out on:
explanation: III.15 Funds & CPPS — CPPS went live across all 122 ROs on 1 Jan 2025. Enables pension credit to any bank account in India without bank-branch mapping.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Beneficiaries of CPPS at rollout were approximately:
explanation: III.15 Funds & CPPS — ~70 lakh EPS pensioners benefit from the CPPS rollout.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Nomination under EPS is made in:
explanation: III.16 Nomination — Form 2 (Revised) is used for EPS nomination. Must be submitted at time of joining.

subject: EPS 1995

options.option_text: Service rendered during which no EPS contribution was paid

explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Both periods are excluded. Only eligible-service + contribution period counts, up to age 58.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: If member's past service (pre-16 Nov 1995) exceeds specified years, past-service pension is computed using:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Table A/B handles past-service conversion; Table C handles early-pension reduction factors; Table D is withdrawal benefit.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Table B was amended (14 June 2024) to extend factors up to how many years of service?
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Pre-amendment Table B went up to 24 years; amendment extended to 42 years — fairer for long-service members.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: An international worker posted to India by a foreign employer:

options.option_text: Must contribute to EPS on full salary (no ₹15,000 cap)

explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — International workers (IWs) — except those from SSA countries — contribute on full salary without ceiling. Withdrawal restrictions apply.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Social Security Agreements (SSAs) signed by India are primarily for:

options.option_text: Totalisation & exemption of social security contributions for workers posted abroad

explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — SSAs allow detached workers to avoid dual social security contribution and allow exportability of benefits. India has SSAs with 20+ countries.

subject: EPS 1995
explanation: III.17 Pension Disbursement — PPO is a 12-digit number issued by EPFO on pension sanction — gateway to all pension services.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Digital Life Certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) is required:
explanation: III.17 Pension Disbursement — Pensioners must submit Jeevan Pramaan annually (ideally by November, valid till October next year). CPPS + face auth enables easy submission.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: If EPS member leaves service before 10 years and does NOT withdraw, what option exists to retain EPS eligibility?
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Form 10C: member can get a Scheme Certificate that preserves EPS service; can be surrendered later if re-employment in EPS-covered establishment occurs.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: The denominator '70' in pension formula represents:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — '70' is an actuarial constant chosen when EPS was designed, for simplification — no deeper meaning attributed in scheme language.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Higher pension option requires member to deposit:

options.option_text: Only balance contribution on actual wage
Principal arrears of EPS contribution (difference) with interest

explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — Member must deposit the principal arrears on actual salary + interest, routed from EPF balance where possible.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: In the absence of nomination, EPS benefit on death of member goes to:

options.option_text: Widow/widower and children under Scheme definition
Any person claiming through succession certificate only

explanation: III.16 Nomination — EPS is non-testamentary — family as defined in scheme (widow/widower, children) is entitled by operation of Scheme, even without nomination.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Two-year deferment bonus (pension increases by 4% for each year deferred):
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — A member can defer pension beyond 58 up to 60; pension increases by 4% per year (or 8% max) — small but legally available incentive.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Pensionable service is capped at how many years for normal pension calculation?

options.option_text: No statutory cap (practical max ~38 with bonus)

explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — No explicit cap in scheme — but effective service is 38 yrs (20-58) + 2 bonus, limited by tables' factors. Amendments in Jun 2024 extended tables to 42 yrs.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Employees of Central Govt / State Govt with separate pension rules:

options.option_text: Are excluded from EPS (GPF / NPS applies)

explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — Central/State govt employees are governed by CCS (Pension) Rules, NPS (post 2004), or GPF — not EPS. However PSU employees may fall under EPS if establishment is covered.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: 'Higher Pension' arrears, once computed, are paid:

options.option_text: Via adjustment against EPF corpus + credit of difference

explanation: III.17 Pension Disbursement — Higher pension arrears are debited from member's EPF balance (where sufficient); deficit demanded separately; surplus credited back. Monthly pension is revised prospectively.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: A member with 12 years 8 months pensionable service — for pension calculation, 'service' is taken as:
explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — Fraction of ≥6 months is rounded up to next full year; <6 months is ignored — Para 10.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: If widow remarries, widow pension is:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Widow pension is payable for the lifetime of the widow/widower — remarriage does NOT cut it off (post-scheme liberalisation).

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Which of the following periods does NOT count as pensionable service?

options.option_text: Period during which no EPS contribution was paid
Period of strike treated as dies non

explanation: III.12 Pension Formula — All three periods are excluded from pensionable service as no contribution was paid.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Investment pattern of EPS corpus is decided by:
explanation: III.15 Funds & CPPS — Investment pattern for non-Govt PF / EPS / EDLI is notified by Ministry of Finance. Includes Govt securities, corporate bonds, equity (via ETFs), etc.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Equity investment by EPFO began with:
explanation: III.15 Funds & CPPS — EPFO started investing in equity via CPSE ETFs in 2015; pattern now permits up to 15% in equity ETFs (Nifty 50, Sensex, CPSE, Bharat 22).

subject: EPS 1995

options.option_text: If member has no widow/child, dependent father/mother gets pension

explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — If there is no widow/child eligible, dependent parents get pension (father first, else mother) at 50% of member's pension, for life.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Madras HC in BHEL Trichy (Sep 2025) ruled:

options.option_text: EPF exemption extends to EPS automatically
EPF exemption does NOT automatically exempt EPS; separate EPS exemption needed

explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — Madras HC: Even if an establishment is exempted from EPF under S.17, it must have separate notification for EPS exemption — not automatic.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: EPS membership for an employee who joined EPF BEFORE 16 Nov 1995:

options.option_text: Automatic — past service benefit computed via Table A/B

explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — Pre-16-Nov-1995 Family Pension Scheme members were automatically converted to EPS members; past service pension computed through Tables A and B.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Maximum number of child pensions payable simultaneously is:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Maximum 2 child pensions at any time; on cessation (age 25 or marriage), next eligible child moves up in the queue.

subject: EPS 1995
explanation: III.17 Pension Disbursement — Form 10D: application for monthly pension under EPS 1995 by a member on retirement / superannuation.

subject: EPS 1995

options.option_text: Withdrawal benefit / Scheme Certificate under EPS (<10 years)

explanation: III.17 Pension Disbursement — Form 10C: withdrawal benefit (lump sum) or Scheme Certificate for members with <10 yrs service.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: A member joining EPF AFTER 1 Sep 2014 with wages >₹15,000 is:

options.option_text: Not eligible for EPS (even with employer consent)

explanation: III.11 EPS Applicability — New members joining EPF after 1 Sep 2014 with wages >₹15,000 are NOT eligible for EPS at all — entire 12% + 12% goes to EPF.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: The EPS 1995 amendment dated 22 August 2014 (effective 1 Sep 2014) changed:

options.option_text: Pensionable Salary averaging from 12 to 60 months
Closed new entry for those above ₹15,000

explanation: III.14 Higher Pension — All three changes came into effect from 1 Sep 2014 under a single amendment; subject of Sunil Kumar case.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: Maximum pension under the existing cap (₹15,000 salary × 35 yrs / 70) is approximately:
explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — 15000 × 35/70 = 7500 (normal). With 2 bonus years: 15000 × 40/70 = 8,571. For higher-pension members (actual salary), pension could be much higher.

subject: EPS 1995
stem: In case of 'death while in service', a widow is entitled to:

options.option_text: Widow pension (service deemed 10 yrs) + EDLI benefit + EPF balance

explanation: III.13 Types of Pension — Death-in-service triggers: (1) widow/child pension under EPS, (2) EDLI insurance up to ₹7 lakh, (3) EPF balance with interest. All three are payable.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — EDLI came into force on 1 August 1976 under S.6C of EPF Act. Replaced earlier insurance schemes run by private insurers for EPF members.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — Only the employer pays EDLI contribution — 0.5% of wages capped at ₹15,000 (max ₹75/month). No employee contribution.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: EDLI admin charges paid by employer are:
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — EDLI admin charges: 0.01% of wages (minimum ₹200/month). Kept separate from EPF admin charges (0.5%).

subject: EDLI 1976

options.option_text: 30 × monthly wages + bonus (50% of avg PF balance, max ₹1.75 lakh)

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Benefit = 30 × avg monthly wages of last 12 months (capped ₹15,000) + 50% of average EPF balance of last 12 months (max ₹1,75,000).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: The MAXIMUM EDLI benefit payable (as permanently extended Oct 2024) is:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Maximum ₹7 lakh — permanent extension notified Oct 2024 (earlier interim since 2021).

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Minimum insurance benefit: ₹2,50,000 — payable if member had 12 months continuous service in EPF-covered establishments.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: To claim maximum EDLI benefit, minimum continuous service required is:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — 12 months continuous EPF membership (can be across multiple employers, if UAN-linked) is required for full benefit.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Form 5(IF) is the claim form for EDLI benefit. Filed by nominee/legal heir with death certificate and other documents.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: An employer can seek exemption from EDLI if:

options.option_text: He runs a similar insurance scheme with benefits not less favourable to employees

explanation: IV.20 Exemption — S.17(2A): exemption from EDLI permitted if employer has a group insurance scheme with benefits not less favourable than EDLI (subject to RPFC certification).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: EDLI benefit is payable only when member dies:

options.option_text: While in employment of EPF-covered establishment (death-in-service)

explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — EDLI covers death WHILE in employment of an EPF-covered establishment. Death after cessation of employment is not covered.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: If member worked 10 months and died, EDLI benefit is:

options.option_text: Minimum ₹2.5 lakh (not eligible for max ₹7 lakh because <12 months)

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Less than 12 months service means eligibility for full cap is not met — only the formula amount (30×wage + bonus) applies; minimum ₹2.5 lakh minimum clause requires 12 months service.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: In the bonus component '50% of avg EPF balance', the average is of the last:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Average EPF balance over the last 12 months immediately preceding the month of death is used.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: For an employee with ₹18,000 basic wage (above ceiling), the 30×wage component of EDLI is:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Wages for EDLI are capped at ₹15,000 even if actual salary is higher; therefore 30 × 15,000 = ₹4,50,000 is the maximum wage component.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — EDLI is a pure death-in-service insurance; no disability, hospitalisation, or maturity benefit.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: A private group insurance exempting employer from EDLI must include:

options.option_text: Coverage not less than statutory EDLI

explanation: IV.20 Exemption — To qualify for EDLI exemption, private scheme must give benefits NOT LESS FAVOURABLE than statutory EDLI — otherwise exemption denied.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Bonus component max of ₹1,75,000 was fixed w.e.f.:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Bonus component max increased to ₹1,75,000 w.e.f. 28-Apr-2021 (from ₹1,50,000 earlier).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Prior to Oct 2024, the ₹7 lakh cap was:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — ₹7 lakh cap was interim (notified 28-Apr-2021, extended from time to time). Oct 2024 notification made it permanent — no more sunset clause.

subject: EDLI 1976

options.option_text: Exempt from tax under S.10(10D) of IT Act

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — EDLI death benefit is treated as life insurance receipts — exempt under S.10(10D) of IT Act (sum received from life insurance on death).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: If no nomination is filed under EDLI, benefit is paid to:
explanation: IV.21 EDLI Claim Process — In absence of nomination, benefit goes to legal heirs (widow, children, parents) based on personal law / succession certificate.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Recent trend for EDLI maximum cap was:

options.option_text: Was ₹6L then raised to ₹7L (Apr 2021, permanent Oct 2024)

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Cap evolution: ₹3.6L → ₹6L → ₹7L (Apr 2021, interim) → ₹7L (permanent Oct 2024).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Admin charges for EDLI have a MINIMUM per month of:
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — Minimum EDLI admin charges are ₹200/month (or ₹25/month for non-functional establishments).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Exemption from EDLI is granted by:

options.option_text: Central Govt after considering CBT recommendation

explanation: IV.20 Exemption — Under S.17(2A), exemption from EDLI is granted by Central Govt (after CBT recommendation).

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: Claim for EDLI must be filed within what period after death?

options.option_text: No time limit — but delay affects investigation

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — No statutory time bar; practical guidance says claim should be filed as soon as possible; delay may require submission of reasons.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: The '50% bonus' is computed as 50% of avg EPF balance or maximum:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Bonus = 50% of avg EPF balance of last 12 months, capped at ₹1,75,000.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.20 Exemption — Exempted employers pay an inspection charge of 0.005% (reduced from 0.01%) instead of full contribution. This is notional cost for EPFO's oversight.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: An EDLI claim is settled and paid through:

options.option_text: EPFO (directly to nominee/legal heirs' bank account)

explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — Post claim approval by EPFO RO, benefit is directly credited to nominee/legal heirs' bank account. Employer is not in the payment loop.

subject: EDLI 1976

options.option_text: All 'employees' as defined in S.2(f) of EPF Act

explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — All 'employees' under the EPF Act definition are automatically EDLI members (no separate enrollment) — including contract labour on establishment rolls.

subject: EDLI 1976
explanation: IV.18 EDLI Basics — S.6C of EPF Act (inserted by 1976 amendment) authorises framing of EDLI Scheme.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: For a member with last 12 months wages averaging ₹15,000 and average PF balance ₹4 lakh:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — 30 × 15,000 = 4,50,000 + min(2,00,000, 1,75,000) = 1,75,000 → total 6,25,000. Maximum cap of 7L not reached here because 6.25L < 7L.

subject: EDLI 1976
stem: If a member with 12 months service dies and formula yields ₹1,80,000, minimum payable is:
explanation: IV.19 Benefit Formula — Formula amount is topped up to minimum ₹2.5 lakh when member had 12+ months continuous service; otherwise formula amount paid.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: The Code on Social Security, 2020 received Presidential assent on:
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — The Code on Social Security 2020 got presidential assent on 28 September 2020 (Gazette Notification No. 48 of 2020).

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Major provisions of the SS Code came into force on:
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — Gazette Notification No. S.O. 5319(E) dated 21 November 2025 enforced most operative provisions of the SS Code — five years after assent.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: How many central labour laws are consolidated by the SS Code, 2020?
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — The SS Code consolidates 9 central labour enactments on social security.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Which of the following is NOT subsumed by the SS Code, 2020?
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — ID Act 1947 is subsumed by the Industrial Relations Code 2020, not the SS Code. The SS Code absorbs EPF, ESI, Gratuity, Maternity, Employees' Compensation, BOCW, ISMW, UOW and BOCW Cess.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, gratuity qualifying service for Fixed Term Employees (FTE) is:
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — For FTEs, gratuity is payable after 1 year of continuous service — liberalisation compared to 5 years under Payment of Gratuity Act 1972.

subject: SS Code 2020

options.option_text: A person engaged in work arrangements outside traditional employer-employee relationship and earning from such activities

explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — S.2(35) SS Code defines gig worker broadly. Platform workers are a subset operating through online platforms.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, aggregators (e.g. ride-hailing, food delivery) contribute to social security for gig workers at:

options.option_text: 1-2% of annual turnover (max 5% of amount paid to gig workers)

explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — S.114(4): aggregators contribute 1-2% of annual turnover (max 5% of amount paid to gig workers). Exact rate to be notified.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: A new Social Security Fund is set up under SS Code for:
explanation: V.25 Benefits — S.141 sets up a Social Security Fund to provide benefits (accident, health, maternity, old age) to gig and platform workers.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, national-level boards for unorganised workers are constituted at:
explanation: V.25 Benefits — S.6: National Social Security Board at Centre + State Unorganised Workers' Social Security Boards in each State.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, ESI will cover:

options.option_text: All workers in factories with 10+ workers

explanation: V.26 ESIC under Code — ESI applicability extended to establishments with 10+ workers and all notified employments. Under original ESI Act, it was 10 or 20 depending on State rules.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: ESI wage ceiling (as per notification under ESI Act/Code) is currently:
explanation: V.26 ESIC under Code — ESI wage ceiling is ₹21,000/month (₹25,000 for persons with disability) — contribution: employee 0.75% + employer 3.25%.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: SS Code retains EPF wage ceiling at:
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — SS Code does NOT explicitly mention wage ceilings; these will be notified under rules. Expected to remain ₹15,000 initially.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Maternity Benefit under SS Code is:

options.option_text: 26 weeks for first two children (12 weeks for third+)

explanation: V.25 Benefits — 26 weeks for first two children (of which ≤8 weeks pre-delivery); 12 weeks for third and subsequent children. Adopting mother: 12 weeks.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Crèche facility under Code applies to establishments with:
explanation: V.25 Benefits — Establishments with 50+ employees must provide crèche facility — either at workplace or within a prescribed distance. Mothers entitled to 4 visits/day.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Code prescribes a single registration portal for employer registration — called:
explanation: V.27 Compliance — Shram Suvidha is the integrated labour portal for registration, returns, and inspections across all labour enactments/codes.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, Inspector is redesignated as:
explanation: V.27 Compliance — SS Code redesignates Inspectors as 'Inspector-cum-Facilitators', combining enforcement with advisory function — aligned with ease of doing business.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Employees' Compensation under SS Code replaces:
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — Workmen's Compensation Act 1923 (renamed Employees' Compensation Act 2009) is subsumed by SS Code — provides lump-sum compensation for employment-related injuries/death.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, workers of what category now also get registration rights:
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — Major innovation: gig, platform, and unorganised workers can register on e-Shram portal and access statutory welfare schemes.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Gratuity under SS Code continues to be calculated at:

options.option_text: 15 days' wages per year of service

explanation: V.25 Benefits — Code retains: 15 days/year for non-seasonal establishments; 7 days/year for seasonal — same as original Gratuity Act 1972.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Maximum gratuity payable under SS Code is:

options.option_text: ₹20 lakh (Govt servant rules; CBT has raised to 25L)
₹25 lakh (Central Govt servants only, 1-Jan-2024; private remains ₹20L)

explanation: V.25 Benefits — Central Govt raised gratuity ceiling to ₹25 lakh in Apr 2024 (under notification). Earlier ₹20 lakh since 2018 (Gratuity Amendment Act). For private sector: notified ceiling applies.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Penalty for first offence of non-payment of any contribution under SS Code is:

options.option_text: Imprisonment 1-3 years + fine up to ₹1 lakh

explanation: V.27 Compliance — SS Code penalties: contribution default = imprisonment 1-3 years + fine up to ₹1 lakh. Repeat offence: 2-5 years + fine up to ₹3 lakh.

subject: SS Code 2020

options.option_text: ID Act, Trade Unions Act, IE (Standing Orders) Act

explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — IR Code combines: Industrial Disputes Act 1947, Trade Unions Act 1926, and Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act 1946.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: How many labour codes did India enact (2019-2020 reform)?
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — Four codes: (1) Code on Wages 2019, (2) IR Code 2020, (3) SS Code 2020, (4) OSH (Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions) Code 2020.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Code on Wages, 2019 got presidential assent on:
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — Code on Wages 2019 (first of the four labour codes) was assented on 8 August 2019.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Which enactment is NOT consolidated into SS Code?
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — Minimum Wages Act is subsumed into the Code on WAGES, 2019, not SS Code.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under ESI: employer contribution rate is:
explanation: V.26 ESIC under Code — Employer: 3.25% of wages; employee: 0.75% → total 4% of wages.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, unorganised workers receive social security through:

options.option_text: Schemes framed by Central/State Govt under Code

explanation: V.25 Benefits — S.109 empowers Central/State Govt to frame welfare schemes for unorganised workers covering life, disability, health, maternity, old age, housing, education.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: e-Shram portal (for unorganised workers) was launched in:
explanation: V.25 Benefits — e-Shram portal was launched by Ministry of Labour in August 2021. Provides UAN (Universal Account Number) for unorganised workers. Over 30 crore registrations.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Under SS Code, Compounding of offences (non-imprisonable) is allowed at:
explanation: V.27 Compliance — Offences (not punishable by imprisonment only) can be compounded for 50% of maximum fine prescribed.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Social Security Fund for gig workers is administered by:

options.option_text: National Social Security Board or a specialised body

explanation: V.25 Benefits — The SS Fund is administered by the National Social Security Board (or a specialised agency) as prescribed.

subject: SS Code 2020
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — FTE as a formal category was first introduced by Standing Orders amendment 2018, then given statutory recognition in IR Code 2020 and SS Code 2020.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Does SS Code require separate SS registration for gig workers?
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — Gig/platform workers must register on e-Shram; their data + aggregator contribution data feeds into the Social Security Fund.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: 'Social Security' is defined in SS Code as:

options.option_text: Measures to ensure income security and access to healthcare

explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — S.2(78) defines 'social security' as measures of protection for workers to ensure income security and healthcare — covers all schemes under the Code.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: ESIC dispensaries and hospitals continue under:
explanation: V.26 ESIC under Code — ESIC operates its own network of hospitals, dispensaries, and tie-up hospitals — administered by ESI Corporation.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: 'Wages' under SS Code excludes which of the following?
explanation: V.25 Benefits — Definition of wages in Code on Wages & SS Code excludes conveyance allowance, HRA, OT, commission, bonus etc., BUT if excluded allowances exceed 50% of total, the excess is treated as wages.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: An FTE terminated on expiry of fixed term is NOT entitled to:
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — FTEs whose contract naturally expires are NOT entitled to retrenchment compensation (contract termination is not retrenchment under ID Act/IR Code).

subject: SS Code 2020

options.option_text: A digital intermediary connecting services-buyers with service-providers

explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — S.2(2) defines Aggregator as a digital intermediary or marketplace connecting buyers of services with service providers. Nine classes of aggregators listed in Seventh Schedule.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Which is listed as an 'aggregator' class in Seventh Schedule of SS Code?
explanation: V.24 Scope & Coverage — Seventh Schedule lists aggregators: ride-sharing, food/grocery delivery, logistics, e-market-place, professional services, healthcare, travel & hospitality, content & media, and other goods/services.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Inspector-cum-Facilitator may be provided inspection plan / risk-based scheme by:
explanation: V.27 Compliance — Central or State Govt (as 'appropriate government') may notify inspection schemes — may specify risk-based, random, or computer-generated visits.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: The SS Code specifies which technology-backed measure?
explanation: V.25 Benefits — SS Code encourages digitisation: Aadhaar auth, biometrics, portal submissions, digital notices — aligned with Digital India.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: The SS Code replaces which pre-existing body nomenclature?
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — EPFO retains its identity under the Code; continues to administer EPF, EPS, EDLI. ESIC also continues. SSOI is not a real acronym.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Which Chapter of SS Code governs Provident Fund?
explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — Chapter III of SS Code (Sections 15-23) governs EPF, EPS, EDLI schemes — effectively replacing EPF Act 1952 once fully enforced.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Maternity Benefit entitlement applies to establishments employing:
explanation: V.25 Benefits — Maternity Benefit (Chapter VI of SS Code) applies to every shop/establishment employing 10 or more employees.

subject: SS Code 2020
explanation: V.26 ESIC under Code — ESI benefits (medical, sickness, maternity, disability) are available after a contribution period completes — typically 9-10 months depending on benefit type.

subject: SS Code 2020
stem: Nine Acts consolidated by SS Code includes which two compensation laws?

options.option_text: Workmen's Compensation (1923) and Unorganised Workers' SSA (2008)
Both ID Act and TU Act

explanation: V.23 SS Code Overview — Out of 9 Acts consolidated, Workmen's/Employees' Compensation Act 1923 and Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act 2008 are the two compensation/welfare laws.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 came into force on:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — ID Act received assent 11 March 1947 and came into force on 1 April 1947.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.2(s) excludes: (i) persons employed mainly in managerial or administrative capacity, (ii) supervisors drawing wages > ₹10,000/month, and (iii) members of armed forces/police.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Minimum workforce for constitution of a Works Committee under ID Act is:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.3: Every industrial establishment employing 100+ workmen must constitute a Works Committee (equal representation of employer and workmen).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Strike notice under ID Act (public utility service) requires:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.22: 14 days' notice required for strike in public utility service. The strike must also commence within 6 weeks of the notice.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Lay-off compensation under ID Act is:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25C: 50% of basic wages + DA for every day laid off, subject to conditions. Applicable to establishments with 50+ workmen.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Retrenchment compensation under ID Act is:

options.option_text: 7 days' wages per year of service
15 days' wages per year of service

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25F(b): 15 days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Notice period for retrenchment under S.25F is:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25F(a): 1 month notice in writing (or wages in lieu) indicating reasons for retrenchment.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: LIFO principle for retrenchment appears under:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25G requires the employer to retrench the workman who was the last person to be employed — 'last-in-first-out' in the category.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Re-employment preference for retrenched workman is under:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25H: retrenched workman has preference in re-employment for up to 1 year.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Under S.25K (Chapter VB), prior Government permission is needed for retrenchment if workforce exceeds:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Pre-2020: 100 workmen. IR Code 2020 raised the threshold to 300 workmen — needs prior Govt permission for lay-off, retrenchment, or closure.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — ID Act follows graded dispute resolution: (1) Conciliation by Officer, (2) Voluntary Arbitration, (3) Adjudication by Labour Court / Industrial Tribunal / National Tribunal.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: National Industrial Tribunal is constituted by:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.7B: National Tribunal constituted by Central Govt for disputes of national importance or those affecting multiple States.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Minimum Wages Act 1948 prescribes minimum wages for:
explanation: VI.29 Minimum Wages — MW Act applies only to 'scheduled employments' notified by appropriate Govt (Central or State). Currently ~47 scheduled employments by Central Govt.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Minimum wages are fixed / revised by:

options.option_text: Appropriate Govt (Central or State as applicable)

explanation: VI.29 Minimum Wages — S.3: Appropriate Govt fixes minimum wages, usually after consulting Advisory Boards or through Notifications. Revised every 5 years or earlier.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Under Code on Wages 2019, the concept of 'floor wage' is introduced — fixed by:
explanation: VI.29 Minimum Wages — S.9 Code on Wages: Central Govt fixes 'floor wage' considering geographical area, living standards, etc. States cannot fix minimum wages below floor wage.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Payment of Gratuity Act 1972 applies to establishments employing:
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — S.1(3): Gratuity Act applies to every factory/mine/oilfield/plantation/port/railway/shop employing 10 or more persons on any day in the preceding 12 months.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Gratuity is payable after continuous service of:
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — Minimum 5 years of continuous service required — except death/disablement cases where it is waived. FTE qualifying service is 1 year under SS Code.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — Non-seasonal: (Last drawn basic + DA) × 15/26 × completed years. Seasonal: 7 days' wages × completed seasons.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Maximum gratuity payable (post Apr 2024 notification) is:
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — Ceiling raised to ₹25 lakh from ₹20 lakh (8th Pay Commission trigger) — applicable to Govt servants from 1 Jan 2024, notified for private sector soon after.

subject: Labour Laws

options.option_text: Exempt up to notified limit for eligible employees under S.10(10)

explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — Under S.10(10) of IT Act: gratuity up to notified limit (₹20L, now ₹25L) is exempt from income tax for eligible non-govt employees; fully exempt for Govt servants.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Payment of Bonus Act 1965 applies to establishments employing:
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — S.1(3): Bonus Act applies to factories (S.2(m)) and every other establishment employing 20 or more persons on any day during an accounting year.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Wage ceiling for bonus eligibility is:
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — Bonus Act, post 2015 Amendment: wage ceiling ₹21,000/month (raised from ₹10,000). Also bonus computation on notional ₹7,000 or minimum wage, whichever higher.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — S.10: Minimum bonus is 8.33% of annual wages (one month's wage) even if there is no allocable surplus (loss). Maximum 20%.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Allocable surplus in non-banking companies is:
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — S.4, Bonus Act: for non-banking companies, allocable surplus = 67% of available surplus; for banking companies = 60%.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Paid maternity leave (post 2017 amendment) for first two children is:
explanation: VI.32 Maternity — 26 weeks paid leave for first 2 children (of which ≤8 weeks pre-delivery). For 3rd & subsequent: 12 weeks.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Minimum qualifying period for maternity benefit is:
explanation: VI.32 Maternity — Woman must have worked at least 80 days in the 12 months preceding expected date of delivery.

subject: Labour Laws

options.option_text: 12 weeks leave from date of child's handover

explanation: VI.32 Maternity — Commissioning mother: 12 weeks maternity leave from date the child is handed over. Introduced by 2017 amendment.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Nursing breaks under Maternity Benefit Act are:

options.option_text: 2 of 15 mins each until child is 15 months

explanation: VI.32 Maternity — S.11: 2 nursing breaks of 15 minutes each until the child attains age of 15 months — in addition to usual rest intervals.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.2(l): 'Lock-out' = temporary closing of a place of employment, or suspension of work, or refusal by employer to continue to employ persons.

subject: Labour Laws

options.option_text: Cessation of work by a body of persons acting in combination

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.2(q): Strike = 'cessation of work by a body of persons employed in any industry acting in combination, or a concerted refusal ... to accept employment'.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Illegal strike means a strike that is:

options.option_text: In contravention of S.22 or S.23 (notice/prohibition)

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.24: strike/lock-out in contravention of S.22 or S.23 or during pendency of conciliation/adjudication proceedings is illegal.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: 'Industry' under ID Act was expansively defined in:

options.option_text: Bangalore Water Supply vs A. Rajappa (1978, 7-judge bench)

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Bangalore Water Supply (1978): 7-judge bench vastly expanded 'industry' to include hospitals, charities, universities, Govt departments — triple test.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: 'Triple test' laid down in Bangalore Water Supply requires:

options.option_text: Systematic activity + cooperation of employer & employee + production of goods/services

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Triple test: (1) systematic activity, (2) cooperation between employer and employee, (3) for the production/distribution of goods or services calculated to satisfy human wants.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: In Surendra Kumar Verma v. CGIT (1980), SC clarified 'continuous service' as:

options.option_text: 240 days in a year ≡ continuous service

explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — 240 days of actual work in preceding 12 months = 'continuous service' for statutory purposes — applied to retrenchment / gratuity cases.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Labour Court (S.7) adjudicates disputes specified in:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Labour Court jurisdiction — Second Schedule disputes (e.g., propriety of standing orders, dismissal, withdrawal of privileges).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Industrial Tribunal (S.7A) adjudicates disputes specified in:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Industrial Tribunal has broader jurisdiction — Second and Third Schedule (wages, hours of work, rationalisation, retrenchment etc.).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Time limit for making Reference to Adjudication by Appropriate Govt is:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — No statutory limit on reference, but delay must be justified. SC has held long delay makes reference stale (Ajay bhai Shirodkar v. UoI).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Medical Bonus under Maternity Benefit Act is:
explanation: VI.32 Maternity — Medical bonus ₹3,500 — payable if pre/post-natal care is not provided free by employer. Originally ₹250, revised to ₹3,500 in 2011.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Forfeiture of gratuity is permitted if employee's service is terminated for:

options.option_text: Willful misconduct causing damage/loss OR moral turpitude

explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — S.4(6): Gratuity can be forfeited wholly or partially only for: (a) willful omission causing damage/loss/property destruction, (b) riotous/disorderly conduct or moral turpitude.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Eligibility for bonus requires minimum working days in an accounting year of:
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — S.8: Eligibility = worked for not less than 30 working days in the accounting year.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: If employer delays gratuity payment beyond 30 days of due date, he must pay:
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — S.7(3A): Simple interest as notified by Central Govt (currently 10% p.a.) on delay beyond 30 days from date becoming payable.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Standing Orders Act 1946 applies to industrial establishments employing:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Pre-IR Code: 100+ workmen (Central rule). IR Code 2020 raised threshold to 300 for ease of doing business.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: The 'Raptakos Brett' formula (1992 SC) revised components of 'need-based minimum wage':

options.option_text: 3 units + children's education + medical + festivals + old-age

explanation: VI.29 Minimum Wages — In Workmen of Raptakos Brett vs Management (1992), SC added: children's education, medical care, minimum recreation, provision for old-age/marriage — to the 1957 Indian Labour Conf. formula of 3 units.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Controlling Authority under Gratuity Act is:

options.option_text: Labour Commissioner or officer notified by Govt

explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — S.3: Appropriate Govt notifies Controlling Authority (usually Labour Commissioner, Assistant Labour Commissioner).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Set-on and set-off under Bonus Act refer to:

options.option_text: Allocable surplus carried forward (set-on) or backward (set-off) for 4 years

explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — S.15: If allocable surplus exceeds max bonus (20%), excess is 'set on' (carried forward up to 4 years); if deficit, 'set off' from past/future years.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.2(k): dispute / difference between (a) employers and employers, (b) employers and workmen, (c) workmen and workmen — connected with employment or conditions of labour.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: A dispute raised by an individual workman becomes 'industrial dispute' if:

options.option_text: It is espoused by a substantial number of workmen / Union

explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate (1958 SC): individual dispute becomes industrial dispute only when espoused by Union or substantial number of workmen. S.2A added later to cover termination cases.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: S.2A of ID Act (inserted 1965) deems which dispute to be an industrial dispute even without espousal?
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.2A: discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination of an individual workman is automatically deemed an industrial dispute, notwithstanding lack of espousal.

subject: Labour Laws
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — Form F is the nomination form under Payment of Gratuity Act — filed by employee within 30 days of completion of 1 year of service.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Closure notice for a unit with 300+ workmen must be given to Govt:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.25O: 90 days' prior application to Govt for permission to close (Chapter VB — 300+ post IR Code).

subject: Labour Laws
stem: 'Salary or wage' for bonus computation excludes:
explanation: VI.31 Bonus Act — Bonus Act S.2(21): salary excludes OT, commission, HRA, travelling concession, employer's contribution to EPF, gratuity, bonus etc. Retaining allowance is INCLUDED.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Tripartite Advisory Board under Minimum Wages Act has representatives of:

options.option_text: Govt, Employers, Workers in equal numbers

explanation: VI.29 Minimum Wages — S.7 & S.9: Advisory Boards have equal representation of Govt, Employers' associations, and Workers' representatives — tripartite.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Compulsory insurance for gratuity (S.4A) is notified by:
explanation: VI.30 Gratuity Act — S.4A: Every employer covered under Gratuity Act may be required to obtain insurance for liability — notified by appropriate Govt. Enforced in few states only.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Conciliation officer's duties are prescribed in:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — S.12: conciliation officer investigates, mediates, and if settlement reached, reports to Govt; if not, sends failure report.

subject: Labour Laws
stem: Trade Unions Act came into force in:
explanation: VI.28 ID Act 1947 — Trade Unions Act 1926, assented 25 March 1926, enforced 1 June 1927. Subsumed into IR Code 2020.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: The current base year for India's GDP series is:
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — 2011-12 is the base year of the current GDP series (adopted January 2015). CSO is working on revision to 2020-21 base.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + ?
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — GDP(MP) = GDP(FC) + (Net Indirect Taxes) = GDP(FC) + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — GNP = GDP + NFIA (Net Factor Income from Abroad). For India, NFIA is usually negative (more outflow than inflow).

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — Y (GDP) = C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (govt expenditure) + (X-M) (net exports).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Reserve Bank of India was established on:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934. Nationalised on 1 January 1949.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has how many members?
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — MPC has 6 members: Governor (Chair), Deputy Governor (Monetary Policy), one RBI officer, and 3 external members nominated by Central Govt — constituted since Sept 2016.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Current Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is approximately:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — CRR = 4% of Net Demand & Time Liabilities (NDTL) — has been at 4% for most of 2024-25 (briefly 4.5% earlier).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Repo rate in Feb 2026 stood at approximately:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — RBI's repo rate has been 6.25% for most of late 2025-early 2026 (reduced from 6.50% peak of the tightening cycle).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative tool of RBI?
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — Moral suasion is a QUALITATIVE tool (persuasion, consultation). CRR, SLR, Bank Rate, Repo, MSF, OMOs are quantitative tools.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Article of the Constitution relating to Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Article 112: Annual Financial Statement is the Budget of the Union. Laid before Parliament each year. Article 202 is State equivalent.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Article 110: Money Bill definition. Can only be introduced in Lok Sabha on President's recommendation. Rajya Sabha has 14 days to return.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Fiscal deficit (FRBM target for FY 2025-26) is approximately:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Union Budget 2025-26 pegged fiscal deficit at 4.4%; Budget 2026-27 (Feb 2026) further reduces to 4.3%. Glide path from 5.9% post-Covid).

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Revenue deficit = Revenue Expenditure minus Revenue Receipts. Indicates Govt's dissaving on current account.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit minus Interest Payments. Reflects current borrowing needs excluding past interest liabilities.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on:
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — NITI (National Institution for Transforming India) Aayog was set up by executive resolution on 1 January 2015. Chairperson: PM.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: India's per capita income at current prices (FY 24-25 provisional) is approximately:
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — Per capita net national income at current prices: ~₹1.85 lakh (FY 24-25 provisional, NSO). At constant prices: ~₹1.13 lakh.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Consumer Price Index (Combined) current base year is:
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — CPI(C) base: 2024=100 (new series released 12-Feb-2026; earlier 2012). WPI base: 2011-12. IIP base: 2011-12.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: 'Headline inflation' in India is measured by:
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — Since April 2014, RBI follows CPI (Combined) as the 'headline' inflation index, targeting 4% (±2%) under flexible inflation targeting regime.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — Under MPC framework (2016), target: 4% ± 2% = 2% to 6% band. Renewed in 2021 for 5 years.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: First bank to be nationalised in India:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — RBI was the first institution nationalised (1 Jan 1949). Imperial Bank became SBI on 1 July 1955 (not nationalisation per se — SBI Act 1955).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: First tranche of commercial bank nationalisation was on:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — 14 commercial banks nationalised on 19 July 1969. Second tranche: 6 banks on 15 April 1980. Total nationalised banks: 20 (now consolidated to 12 public-sector banks).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Consolidated Fund of India is under:
