explanation: VII.35 Budget — Article 266(1): Consolidated Fund of India — all revenues, loans, and receipts from loan recoveries. Withdrawals require Parliamentary authorisation.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Contingency Fund of India was increased to:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Contingency Fund Corpus was raised from ₹500 crore to ₹30,000 crore in Budget 2021 (FY 21-22) — at disposal of President.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: First fully-public-owned bank was established in:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — SBI (State Bank of India) established 1 July 1955 by SBI Act 1955, succeeding Imperial Bank of India. Fully public-owned.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Gross Capital Formation (GCF) in India is around:
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — GCF/GDP ratio hovers around 30-33% in India — a measure of investment. Higher than global average but below China's 40%.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: GST was introduced in India on:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — GST came into effect on 1 July 2017, subsuming multiple indirect taxes — 101st Constitution Amendment Act (2016) enabled it.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Article 279A: GST Council — Chair: Union Finance Minister, Members: Union MoS Revenue + State FMs. Decisions by 75% weighted vote.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — Stagflation = stagnant growth combined with high inflation — like 1970s oil shock.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — RBI sets inflation target but does NOT set GDP growth target (that's done by Govt / Finance Ministry / NITI). RBI issues currency (except ₹1), manages forex, and acts as Govt's banker.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Direct taxes: income tax, corporate tax, capital gains, STT. Indirect: GST, customs, excise.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' package announced in May 2020 was approximately:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Atmanirbhar Bharat package: ₹20 lakh crore (~10% of GDP), covering RBI measures, Govt spending, and structural reforms.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Highest weight in CPI (Combined) is for:
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — Food & beverages has highest weight in CPI(C): ~45.86% — makes India's headline inflation highly sensitive to food prices.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: HDI (Human Development Index) is published by:
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — Human Development Index (HDI) is published annually by UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) since 1990. Combines life expectancy, education, and GNI per capita.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Financial year in India: 1 April to 31 March. Mentioned in various Acts (IT Act etc.).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: SEBI was given statutory status in:
explanation: VII.34 Banking & RBI — SEBI established as non-statutory body in 1988; given statutory status under SEBI Act 1992.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: The 15th Finance Commission award covers years:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — 15th FC award: 2021-22 to 2025-26 (5 years + 1 interim). Chair: N.K. Singh.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Share of States in Central Taxes recommended by 15th FC is:
explanation: VII.35 Budget — 15th FC (final report, 2020) recommended 41% devolution share (earlier 42% by 14th FC; reduced after J&K; bifurcation).

subject: Indian Economy
stem: India's ranking in World GDP (current $) is (2024-25):
explanation: VII.33 Macro Basics — India overtook Japan to become 4th largest economy in 2024-25 (~$4 trillion nominal GDP). Ranking: USA, China, Germany, India.

subject: Indian Economy
explanation: VII.35 Budget — Article 265: 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.' — fundamental principle of taxation.

subject: Indian Economy
stem: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) base year is:
explanation: VII.36 Inflation — WPI base year: 2011-12 (notified 2017). Measures inflation at producer/wholesale level — used for indexation of certain contracts, not monetary policy target.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Constitution adopted/enacted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day since 2015). Came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to Preamble. Full expression: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Part III (Articles 12-35): Fundamental Rights. Part IV: DPSPs. Part IV-A: Fundamental Duties.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Right to Property was DELETED from Fundamental Rights by:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — 44th Amendment (1978) deleted Article 31 and Article 19(1)(f); made Right to Property a legal right under Article 300A.

subject: Indian Polity

options.option_text: Equality before law & equal protection of laws

explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Article 14: 'State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.'

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Article 19(1) currently protects 6 freedoms: speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession. Originally 7 — 19(1)(f) right to property deleted by 44th Amendment.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Right to form trade unions is protected by:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Article 19(1)(c): right to form associations or unions — foundation of trade union rights in India. Note: no right to strike as FR per se.

subject: Indian Polity

options.option_text: Right to life and personal liberty

explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Article 21: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.' Most expansively interpreted FR (Maneka Gandhi 1978).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in:
explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — Part IV (Articles 36-51) contains DPSPs. Borrowed from Irish Constitution. Non-justiciable but fundamental in governance (Article 37).

subject: Indian Polity

options.option_text: Adequate means of livelihood for all citizens

explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — Article 39(a): State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that citizens, men and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.

subject: Indian Polity

options.option_text: Right to work, education, and public assistance

explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — Article 41: State shall, within limits of its economic capacity, make effective provision for securing right to work, to education, and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — Article 43: State shall endeavour to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation, to all workers agricultural, industrial or otherwise, work, a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Article 43A was added by 42nd Amendment and relates to:

options.option_text: Workers' participation in management of industries

explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — Article 43A: State shall take steps to secure the participation of workers in management of undertakings/industrial establishments. Inserted by 42nd Amendment 1976.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Article 39A (Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid) was added by:
explanation: VIII.38 DPSPs — 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Articles 39A, 43A, 48A, 51A among others.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Minimum age to contest Lok Sabha election is:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 84(b): minimum age for Lok Sabha = 25 years. Rajya Sabha: 30 years. Panchayat: 21 (State law typically).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Lok Sabha maximum strength as per Constitution is:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 81: Maximum 552 — 530 States + 20 UTs + 2 Anglo-Indian nominated (last one ended 2020 via 104th Amendment). Current: 543 elected members.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 80: 250 max = 238 elected from States/UTs + 12 nominated by President (from fields of literature, science, art, social service).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Labour is included in which List of Seventh Schedule?
explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — Labour is in Concurrent List (List III), Entry 22. Both Centre and States can legislate; Centre prevails in case of repugnance. Hence EPF Act is a Central Act.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Entry 24 of List III relates to:

options.option_text: Labour welfare (conditions of work, provident funds, employer's liability)

explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — Entry 24 List III: 'Welfare of labour including conditions of work, provident funds, employers' liability, workmen's compensation, invalidity and old age pensions and maternity benefits.' — constitutional basis for EPF Act 1952.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: The Basic Structure Doctrine was laid down in:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (24 Apr 1973): 13-judge bench, 7:6 majority, held Parliament cannot amend Basic Structure of Constitution. Cornerstone constitutional doctrine.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Fundamental Duties were added to Constitution by:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Part IV-A (Article 51A): inserted by 42nd Amendment based on Swaran Singh Committee — originally 10 duties, 11th added by 86th Amendment (education of child).

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Article 368: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution. Three procedures: simple, special, and special + State ratification.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 75(3): Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People) — cornerstone of parliamentary democracy.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award. Param Vir Chakra is the highest military gallantry award (wartime).

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Part XVIII (Articles 352-360): Emergency provisions — National (352), State/President's Rule (356), Financial (360).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: How many Schedules are there in the Constitution (as of 2026)?
explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — 12 Schedules currently. 9th Schedule added by 1st Amendment (1951), 12th added by 74th Amendment (1992) for municipalities.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — 73rd Amendment Act 1992 added Part IX (Panchayats) and 11th Schedule (29 subjects devolved). 74th Amendment: Part IX-A (Municipalities) and 12th Schedule.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Right to Education (Article 21A) was added by:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — 86th Amendment Act 2002 inserted Article 21A (Right to Education of children aged 6-14), Article 45 (modified), and Article 51A(k). RTE Act 2009 operationalised it.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Concept of 'Single Citizenship' was borrowed from:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Single citizenship concept borrowed from UK. USA, Canada, Australia have dual citizenship (state + federal).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Federal features of India's Constitution are:
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — All are federal features. However, India is a 'quasi-federal' or 'federation with unitary bias' — unitary in emergencies.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Attorney General of India is appointed under:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 76: President appoints AG who holds office during pleasure of President. Highest law officer of India.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Comptroller and Auditor-General (CAG) is appointed under:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 148: President appoints CAG. Six-year term or till 65 years, whichever earlier. Removed only by address of Parliament (same as SC Judge).

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Election Commission of India is constituted under:
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 324: Superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in Election Commission (CEC + Election Commissioners). Independent body.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980) held:

options.option_text: DPSPs are subordinate to FRs always
Amending power is limited by Basic Structure
FRs and DPSPs together form basic structure; harmony must be maintained

explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — Minerva Mills (1980): SC struck down 42nd Amendment provisions; held FRs and DPSPs are complementary and together form basic structure. 13:0 bench.

subject: Indian Polity

options.option_text: Land reform and certain State laws from judicial review

explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — 9th Schedule (added 1st Amendment 1951): laws placed here are immune from challenge for FR violation — BUT post I.R. Coelho (2007) SC can review even 9th Schedule laws for Basic Structure compatibility.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — 10th Schedule (inserted by 52nd Amendment 1985): disqualification on ground of defection. Speaker/Chairman decides under 10th Schedule.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Which Amendment made 'Right to Education' a Fundamental Right?
explanation: VIII.37 Constitution — 86th Amendment (2002): Article 21A — Right to Education of children 6-14 years. RTE Act 2009 followed.

subject: Indian Polity
stem: Anti-defection law — a member is disqualified for:

options.option_text: Voluntarily giving up membership of party
Voting against party whip without prior permission

explanation: VIII.40 Schedules — 10th Schedule: defection grounds include voluntary resignation, violating whip, etc. Original 1/3 split exemption removed by 91st Amendment; now 2/3 merger required.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 263: President may establish Inter-State Council. Constituted by Presidential order 28 May 1990 — forum for Centre-State dialogue.

subject: Indian Polity
explanation: VIII.39 Parliamentary Sys — Article 110(3): Speaker of Lok Sabha certifies a bill as Money Bill. His decision is final and not ordinarily subject to judicial review (Roger Matthew, 2019).

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity (Capital). Also expressed as A = L + E. Foundation of double-entry book-keeping.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver
Debit all expenses, Credit all incomes
Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Personal A/c — Debit the Receiver, Credit the Giver. Real A/c — Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out. Nominal A/c — Debit expenses/losses, Credit incomes/gains.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Debit what comes in / Credit what goes out

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Real accounts = tangible assets (Cash, Machinery, Stock). Golden rule: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Debit what comes in / Credit what goes out
Debit expenses & losses / Credit incomes & gains

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Nominal accounts = incomes, expenses, gains, losses. Rule: Debit expenses/losses, Credit incomes/gains.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Each transaction affects only one account
Each transaction has debit and credit effect in at least two accounts

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Double-entry: every transaction has dual aspect — recorded as a debit in one account and a credit in another. Sum of debits = sum of credits.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Revenues matched with the period's expenses that produced them

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Matching concept: expenses incurred to earn revenue of a period are matched with that revenue in the same period — basis of accrual accounting.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Revenue/expense recognised when earned/incurred, regardless of cash receipt

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Accrual basis recognises revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, matching them to the period — not dependent on cash flow timing.

subject: Accounting
stem: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental accounting assumption?
explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Three fundamental assumptions per AS-1: Going Concern, Consistency, Accrual. Conservatism (prudence) is a PRINCIPLE, not fundamental assumption.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Financial position at a point in time

explanation: IX.42 Statements — Balance Sheet is a statement of financial position at a specific date — showing assets, liabilities, and equity. P&L; is for a period.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Performance over a period (income, expenses, profit/loss)

explanation: IX.42 Statements — P&L; Account / Income Statement: performance for a period (month/quarter/year) — revenues, expenses, and net profit/loss.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Check arithmetical accuracy of ledger balances

explanation: IX.42 Statements — Trial Balance lists all ledger balances to verify debits = credits. Starting point for preparing financial statements.

subject: Accounting
stem: Cash Flow Statement classifies activities into:
explanation: IX.42 Statements — AS-3 / Ind AS 7 requires classification into three: Operating, Investing, and Financing activities. May use direct or indirect method for operating activities.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Non-cash expense — allocation of asset cost over useful life

explanation: IX.42 Statements — Depreciation is non-cash — a systematic allocation of the cost of a tangible asset (less residual value) over its useful life.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.42 Statements — SLM: (Cost - Scrap) / Useful Life = constant annual depreciation. Simplest and most commonly used method.

subject: Accounting
stem: Written Down Value (WDV) / Diminishing Balance method charges:

options.option_text: Decreasing amount each year (% on opening book value)

explanation: IX.42 Statements — WDV method applies constant rate (%) on reducing (book) balance → decreasing charge each year. Required under IT Act for most assets.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — Current Ratio = Current Assets ÷ Current Liabilities. Ideal: 2:1. Measures short-term liquidity.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid Expenses) / Current Liabilities. Ideal: 1:1. Stricter liquidity measure.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — Debt-Equity = Long-term Debt ÷ Shareholders' Equity. Indicates financial leverage. Lower = safer; higher = more leveraged.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — GP Ratio = (Gross Profit ÷ Sales) × 100. Measures basic operating efficiency.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — ROCE = (EBIT / Capital Employed) × 100. Capital Employed = Total Assets - Current Liabilities. Key profitability metric.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Anticipate no profit but provide for all losses

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Conservatism: record all anticipated losses but not anticipated profits. Basis of valuing inventory at 'cost or NRV, whichever lower'.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.42 Statements — Contingent liabilities (possible obligations depending on future events) are disclosed as notes / footnotes, not recognised in Balance Sheet itself (AS-29 / Ind AS 37).

subject: Accounting
stem: AS (Accounting Standards) in India are issued by:
explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — ICAI issues AS; MCA notifies for companies (including Ind AS for specified class). Small entities may use ASSE/AS-SMEs.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Business is separate from its owner

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Business Entity concept: business is a separate accounting entity distinct from its owner(s). Owner's personal transactions are NOT mixed with business.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: All transactions recorded in monetary terms

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Only transactions expressible in monetary terms are recorded. Non-monetary items (like employee skills, management quality) are NOT recognised.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Going Concern: entity will continue in operation for the foreseeable future — enables historical cost accounting, deferral of expenses, etc.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.42 Statements — FIFO: oldest stock (first purchased) is issued first. Closing inventory reflects latest purchase prices. In inflation, gives higher profit.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.42 Statements — Ind AS 2 / AS 2 Inventories: permissible methods are FIFO and Weighted Average Cost. LIFO is NOT permitted.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory. Higher = faster movement / efficient stock management. Measured in 'times'.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: There is a difference in Trial Balance — to temporarily balance it

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Suspense A/c holds the difference temporarily until errors are located. Once all errors found, Suspense A/c should vanish.

subject: Accounting
stem: In Receipts and Payments A/c (for NPO):

options.option_text: Only cash transactions (both capital and revenue)

explanation: IX.42 Statements — Receipts and Payments A/c is a real (cash) account — records ALL cash receipts and payments, both capital and revenue nature.

subject: Accounting
stem: Income & Expenditure Account for a non-profit organisation is equivalent to:
explanation: IX.42 Statements — Income & Expenditure A/c serves as P&L; equivalent for NPOs — records revenue items on accrual basis; surplus = excess of income over expenditure.

subject: Accounting
explanation: IX.43 Ratios — Debtors Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Average Debtors (incl. B/R). Higher ratio = faster collection. Inverse: Debt Collection Period.

subject: Accounting
stem: Treatment of bad debts already written off but recovered later:
explanation: IX.42 Statements — Recovery of bad debts written off earlier is credited to P&L; — treated as unexpected income.

subject: Accounting

options.option_text: Entry with more than one debit or credit
Entry in more than one book

explanation: IX.41 Fundamentals — Compound journal entry: involves more than two accounts (more than one debit or credit), but total debit still equals total credit.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: India's first war of independence began at:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Indian sepoys at Meerut cantonment started the revolt on 10 May 1857 — spread to Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi. British crushed it by 1858; Govt of India Act 1858 followed.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Indian National Congress was founded in:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — INC founded at Bombay in Dec 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume. First President: W.C. Bonnerjee.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Partition of Bengal took place in:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal on 16 Oct 1905 on 'administrative' grounds. Sparked Swadeshi and Boycott movements. Annulled in 1911.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms): introduced separate electorates for Muslims, expanded legislative councils. Communally divisive but early step in representative govt.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi): Brig. Gen. Reginald Dyer ordered firing on unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar; 379+ killed. Triggered Non-Cooperation Movement.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — NCM launched in September 1920 (Calcutta Congress); officially from 1 Aug 1920 (day of Tilak's death). Suspended after Chauri Chaura incident (Feb 1922).

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Dandi March / Salt Satyagraha began on:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Gandhi began Dandi March on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram. Covered 385 km in 24 days; broke salt law on 6 April 1930 at Dandi.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — GoI Act 1935: introduced Provincial Autonomy (11 provinces), envisaged federation (never implemented due to princely states' resistance), expanded franchise. Source of much of India's Constitution.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Quit India Movement was launched on:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — AICC passed Quit India resolution on 8 Aug 1942 at Bombay; Gandhi gave 'Do or Die' call on 9 Aug 1942. Leaders arrested overnight; movement spread spontaneously.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Cabinet Mission came to India in:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Cabinet Mission (Stafford Cripps, Pethick-Lawrence, A.V. Alexander) arrived in March 1946. Proposed 3-tier structure; rejected by Muslim League leading to Partition.

subject: History & Labour Movement

options.option_text: Partition of India and transfer of power by 15 Aug 1947

explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Mountbatten Plan announced Partition of India and Pakistan + accelerated transfer to 15 Aug 1947 (earlier scheduled for Jun 1948). Accepted by Congress and League.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Constituent Assembly (Cabinet Mission Plan) began on 9 December 1946, first meeting under Sachchidananda Sinha (interim chair). Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Drafting Committee of Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Drafting Committee (29 Aug 1947) with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as Chairman + 6 members. Key role in framing the Constitution.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: First Factory Act in India was enacted in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Factory Act 1881 was the first labour legislation in British India — regulated child labour (children <7 years), limited work hours, made provision for holidays.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was founded in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — AITUC founded on 31 October 1920, presided by Lala Lajpat Rai. First central trade union body in India. Affiliated to WFTU.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Indian Trade Unions Act was enacted in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Trade Unions Act 1926 (assented 25 March 1926; enforced 1 June 1927). Gave legal recognition and rights to trade unions. Now subsumed into IR Code 2020.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Indian Labour Conference (ILC) was first held in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — ILC (earlier Tripartite Labour Conference) first held in 1942 under Labour Member B.R. Ambedkar's initiative. Tripartite consultative body.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Mines Act was first enacted in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Mines Act 1923 was the first comprehensive legislation for mines in India. Replaced by Mines Act 1952 (still in force).

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: INTUC (Indian National Trade Union Congress) was founded in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — INTUC founded on 3 May 1947 by Indian National Congress under Sardar Patel's guidance. Provides trade union wing for INC.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Workmen's Compensation Act was enacted in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Workmen's Compensation Act 1923 (renamed Employees' Compensation Act by 2009 Amendment). Now subsumed under SS Code 2020.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: First Five-Year Plan was launched in:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — 1st Five-Year Plan: 1951-56 (Harrod-Domar model; focus on agriculture). Planning Commission set up 1950. Replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Gandhi's first Satyagraha on Indian soil was at Champaran (Bihar) in 1917 for indigo peasants against tinkathia system. Success led to Champaran Agrarian Act 1918.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed 5 Mar 1931; Congress agreed to participate in 2nd Round Table Conference; Civil Disobedience suspended. Contested at Karachi Session 1931.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Home Rule Leagues were established by:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Two Home Rule Leagues: B.G. Tilak (April 1916, Maharashtra) and Annie Besant (Sept 1916, Madras). Demanded Home Rule on British dominion pattern.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Simon Commission came to India in:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Simon Commission (1927-28) to review GoI Act 1919; all-British membership (no Indian). Boycotted with 'Simon Go Back' slogan; Lala Lajpat Rai died after police lathi-charge in Lahore.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Nehru Report drafted by Motilal Nehru's committee in 1928 — first blueprint for a Constitution by Indians. Recommended dominion status, fundamental rights.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Poorna Swaraj resolution was passed at:
explanation: X.44 Freedom Struggle — Lahore Congress Dec 1929 (J.L. Nehru President) adopted Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) as the goal. 26 Jan 1930 declared as Independence Day.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Minimum Wages Act came into force on:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Minimum Wages Act 1948 — enacted 15 March 1948, came into force the same day. Sought to secure minimum wages for 'sweated' employments. Now merged into Code on Wages 2019.

subject: History & Labour Movement
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — Employees' State Insurance Act 1948 — first social security legislation in independent India. Provides medical, sickness, maternity, disablement benefits.

subject: History & Labour Movement
stem: Industrial Disputes Act came into force on:
explanation: X.45 Labour Movement — ID Act 1947 came into force on 1 April 1947, repealing Trade Disputes Act 1929. Current statute governing industrial disputes until IR Code is operationalised.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Physics — Force: Newton (N) = kg·m/s². Dyne is CGS unit. Joule: energy. Pascal: pressure.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
explanation: XI.46 Physics — c = 299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum. Universal physical constant.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Physics — F = ma. Alternatively, F = dp/dt (rate of change of momentum). Both formulations equivalent for constant mass.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Chemistry — Carbon's atomic number (Z) = 6 (number of protons). Atomic mass ≈ 12.011.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Chemistry — Dmitri Mendeleev proposed the periodic table in 1869, arranging elements by atomic mass. Modern table arranges by atomic number (H.G.J. Moseley).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Noble gases occupy which group of periodic table?
explanation: XI.46 Chemistry — Group 18 (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn, Og) — noble / inert gases. Fully filled outermost shell.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Human DNA has how many chromosomes?
explanation: XI.46 Biology — Human cells: 46 chromosomes = 23 pairs. 22 pairs of autosomes + 1 pair sex chromosomes (XX female, XY male).

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Biology — CRISPR-Cas9 is a precision genome-editing tool. Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 awarded to Charpentier and Doudna for its discovery.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Biology — Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts (chlorophyll-containing organelles) of plant cells. 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: RBCs (red blood cells) in humans are produced in:
explanation: XI.46 Biology — Red bone marrow (in flat bones like sternum, ribs, vertebrae, hip) is primary site of erythropoiesis in adults. Liver and spleen are sites in foetus.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Space & Tech — Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander touched down near lunar South Pole on 23 August 2023 (18:04 IST). Pragyan rover deployed. 'National Space Day' commemorated annually.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Aditya-L1 (India's first solar mission) was launched on:
explanation: XI.46 Space & Tech — Aditya-L1 launched 2 Sept 2023 by PSLV-C57; reached Lagrangian point L1 (~1.5 million km from Earth) in Jan 2024. Studies Sun's corona and solar wind.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Space & Tech — Gaganyaan: ISRO's human spaceflight program. First uncrewed test 2025; crewed mission planned for 2025-26 with 3 astronauts for 3 days in LEO.

subject: Science & Technology

options.option_text: AI that generates new content (text, image, code)

explanation: XI.46 Technology — Generative AI (like ChatGPT, DALL·E, Claude) creates novel content based on training data. Based on transformer architecture (2017 paper 'Attention is All You Need').

subject: Science & Technology

options.option_text: Distributed ledger technology with cryptographic links

explanation: XI.46 Technology — Blockchain: immutable distributed ledger; each block cryptographically linked. Used in cryptocurrencies, supply chain, smart contracts.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Health — BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) vaccine protects against tuberculosis (TB). Part of India's Universal Immunisation Programme.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Universal blood donor has blood group:
explanation: XI.46 Health — O negative (O-) is universal donor (no A, B, or Rh antigens). AB+ is universal recipient (no anti-A, anti-B, Rh+ antibodies).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: COP-28 (UN Climate Change) was held at:
explanation: XI.46 Environment — COP-28 UNFCCC was held at Dubai, UAE in Nov-Dec 2023. COP-29 at Baku (2024); COP-30 at Belém, Brazil (Nov 2025).

subject: Science & Technology
stem: Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit global warming to:
explanation: XI.46 Environment — Paris Agreement (COP-21, 2015): hold global temperature rise well below 2°C above pre-industrial, and pursue efforts to limit to 1.5°C.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: WHO declared Covid-19 a pandemic on:
explanation: XI.46 Health — WHO declared Covid-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020. India imposed nationwide lockdown from 25 March 2020.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Physics — Ampere (A) is SI unit of electric current. Volt (V): potential difference. Ohm (Ω): resistance. Watt (W): power.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: pH of pure water at 25°C is:
explanation: XI.46 Chemistry — Pure water at 25°C has pH = 7 (neutral). pH < 7 acidic, pH > 7 basic. pH scale 0-14.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Health — Beta cells in Islets of Langerhans (pancreas) produce insulin. Regulates blood glucose. Diabetes = insufficient insulin / insulin resistance.

subject: Science & Technology
stem: ISRO's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was launched in:
explanation: XI.46 Space & Tech — Mangalyaan-1 launched 5 Nov 2013; entered Mars orbit 24 Sep 2014. Made India first Asian and 4th country globally to reach Mars; first to succeed on maiden attempt.

subject: Science & Technology
explanation: XI.46 Physics — Quantum computers use qubits that can exist in superposition (0 and 1 simultaneously) and entanglement — enabling exponentially faster computation for specific problems.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: EPF interest rate for FY 2024-25 was:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — EPF rate 2024-25: 8.25% (retained, CBT meeting Feb 2024). Same 8.25% continued for 2025-26.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: EDLI ₹7 lakh cap was permanently extended in:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — Permanent extension of ₹7 lakh EDLI cap via Gazette notification in October 2024 — earlier was interim since April 2021.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: CPPS (Centralised Pension Payment System) benefits approximately:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — ~70 lakh EPS pensioners benefit from CPPS (launched 1 Jan 2025 across 122 ROs).

subject: Current Affairs
stem: SS Code 2020 major provisions in force date:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — Gazette S.O. 5319(E) dated 21 Nov 2025 enforced major provisions of SS Code 2020 — five years after presidential assent.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Damages under Section 14B / Para 32A, post 15 June 2024, are:

options.option_text: Uniform 1% per month (12% p.a.), no cap
As per 7A officer's discretion up to 5%

explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — Amendment to Para 32A (notified 14 June 2024, effective 15 June 2024) made damages a uniform 1%/month (12% p.a.) with no cap.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Auto-settlement of EPF advance claims was raised to:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — Auto-settlement ceiling raised to ₹5 lakh w.e.f. 24-Jun-2025 (was ₹1 lakh from 30-Nov-2024) — enables claim processing within ~3 days for medical, education, housing, Covid, etc.

subject: Current Affairs
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — UPSC Special Advertisement 52/2025 (dated 29 July 2025) notified 74 APFC + 156 EO/AO = 230 total. Recruitment Test was held on 30 Nov 2025.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: PF Amnesty Scheme was announced at:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — PF Amnesty Scheme announced alongside interest rate decision at 239th CBT (Feb-Mar 2026) — aims to regularise defaults with reduced damages for voluntary compliance.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Table B of EPS was extended in 2024 to cover up to what years of service?
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — 14 June 2024 amendment extended EPS Table B factors up to 42 years of service (earlier 24 years) — benefits long-service members.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Table D of EPS was amended (14 June 2024) to compute withdrawal benefit in:
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — Table D now uses months (not years) — fairer for members with <10 years of service who lose monthly pension eligibility. Pre-amendment, partial years were lost.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Higher Pension applications processed status (Nov 2025 PIB):
explanation: XII.47 EPFO Updates — PIB press release Nov 2025: ~99% of higher-pension applications processed; PPOs issued to 1,24,457+ pensioners; ~12,572 in final stages.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Sunil Kumar vs EPFO (SC) — key date:
explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Sunil Kumar pronounced on 4 November 2022 — upheld eligibility of certain members to opt for higher pension. Validated Sep 2014 amendments with modifications.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Surya Roshni Ltd vs EPFO SC judgment date:
explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Surya Roshni: 28 February 2019. Held universally paid allowances are part of basic wages for EPF. Burden of proof on employer. Set aside UP HC, restored EPFO demand.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Bangalore Water Supply & Sewerage Board vs A. Rajappa — bench size & year:
explanation: XII.48 Judgments — 7-judge bench, 1978 (21 Feb 1978). Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer-led bench gave the expansive 'triple test' for 'industry' under ID Act.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Bridge & Roof Company vs Union of India, year:
explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Bridge & Roof, 1963 SC — laid the 'universally, ordinarily, necessarily paid' test for basic wages under EPF, later applied in Surya Roshni.

subject: Current Affairs

options.option_text: EPF exemption does NOT automatically grant EPS exemption; separate notification needed

explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Madras HC: Even if establishment is exempted from EPF under S.17, separate notification is required for EPS exemption. EPF and EPS are independent schemes.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: RC Gupta vs RPFC (Oct 2016 SC) ruled on:

options.option_text: Right of members to higher pension on actual salary (precursor to Sunil Kumar)

explanation: XII.48 Judgments — RC Gupta (4 Oct 2016): recognised right to contribute on actual wage above ceiling for higher pension; precursor decision to Sunil Kumar (2022).

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Kiran Rajaram Jadhav vs EPFO (Bombay HC, 2026) held:

options.option_text: No higher pension without employer records
EPFO cannot deny higher pension solely due to missing employer records

explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Bombay HC (2026): EPFO set-aside order — employees cannot be denied higher pension solely for missing employer records. Directed EPFO to re-examine such rejections.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: RPFC (II) West Bengal vs Vivekananda Vidyamandir (SC, 28 Feb 2019) held:

options.option_text: Basic wages include all allowances paid universally, necessarily and ordinarily

explanation: XII.48 Judgments — SC delivered Vivekananda (Basic Wages) ruling on 28 Feb 2019 — same day as Surya Roshni. Triggered EPFO's subsequent 14-Feb-2020 guidelines curbing 'roving' 7A enquiries.

subject: Current Affairs
stem: Hindustan Times Ltd v. Union of India (1998) concerned:

options.option_text: 'Regular wages' test for allowances — precursor to Surya Roshni

explanation: XII.48 Judgments — Hindustan Times (1998) SC considered whether allowances were part of regular wages for EPF purposes — developed test later affirmed in Surya Roshni 2019.

subject: Current Affairs

subject: Current Affairs

subject: Mixed Revision

options.option_text: Recommended by CBT, approved by MoF

subject: Mixed Revision

explanation: XIII.49 Mixed Revision — S.7Q is about INTEREST on delayed payment (12% p.a.), not damages. Damages are under S.14B.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Social Security Code 2020?
explanation: XIII.49 Mixed Revision — SS Code DID NOT abolish gratuity — retained and in fact extended it to FTEs after 1 year (vs 5 years pre-Code).

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Monthly EPS pension for an employee with 28 yrs 5 months service, pensionable salary ₹15,000 (no bonus service), is approximately:
explanation: XIII.49 Mixed Revision — Service = 28 years (5 months < 6 is ignored). Pension = (15,000 × 28) / 70 = ₹6,000/month.

subject: Mixed Revision
explanation: XIII.49 Mixed Revision — UAN (Universal Account Number) is unique per member; portable across employers; links multiple Member IDs.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Priority of EPF dues in insolvency is dealt with in:
explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — S.11: EPF dues have priority over other debts except secured creditors. Post IBC, EPF dues are excluded from liquidation estate (Maharashtra State Coop Bank).

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Employer's 12% contribution to EPF is split as:
explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — Standard split: 8.33% to EPS (capped at ₹1,250 on ₹15,000 wage) + 3.67% to EPF.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: In case of death of an EPF member in service, family receives:
explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — On death-in-service: (i) EPS widow/child pension, (ii) EDLI benefit up to ₹7 lakh, (iii) EPF balance with interest — all three trigger together.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Which of the following is a FIT target of RBI (Flexible Inflation Targeting)?
explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — FIT: CPI (Combined) target 4% ± 2% = 2% to 6%. Institutionalised by RBI Act amendment 2016. Renewed 2021.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Right to form trade unions is protected by:
explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — Article 19(1)(c): freedom to form associations/unions. Article 19(1)(a): speech. Article 21: life & liberty. Article 23: against forced labour.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Constitutional entry enabling EPF Act is:

options.option_text: List III, Entry 24 (welfare of labour incl. provident funds)

explanation: XIII.50 High-Yield — List III (Concurrent), Entry 24: 'Welfare of labour including conditions of work, provident funds, employers' liability, workmen's compensation, invalidity and old age pensions, and maternity benefits.'

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: In ZZ vs YY (hypothetical): 'An employer dismissed a worker without notice. ID Act remedy?'
explanation: XIII.51 Judgment Spot — For retrenchment: S.25F requires (i) 1 month notice or wages in lieu and (ii) 15 days' compensation per year of service. Otherwise retrenchment is void ab initio.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Section 7A officer erroneously imposes damages without separate hearing. Is it valid?

explanation: XIII.51 Judgment Spot — S.14B damages require separate quasi-judicial proceeding with opportunity of hearing. Clubbing in a 7A order without separate SCN/hearing is irregular.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Which body comprises (max) 5 Central + 15 State + 10 Employers + 10 Employees reps?

subject: Mixed Revision

explanation: XIII.52 Mock Sampler — 70 is an actuarial design constant in the EPS 1995 formula — no deeper meaning.

subject: Mixed Revision

explanation: XIII.52 Mock Sampler — Interest 12% p.a. (S.7Q) + Damages 12% p.a. (post-Jun-2024 Para 32A, = 1%/month) = effective 24% p.a. load for delayed contribution.

subject: Mixed Revision

D. Chandirasegar v. UoI / BHEL Trichy retirees (Madras HC, Sep 2025)

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: A person above 58 years who continues in an EPF-covered establishment contributes:

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Which of these is a FUNDAMENTAL DUTY (11 in total)?

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

explanation: XIII.53 Final Mock — All three: FTE gratuity after 1 year, Social Security Fund for gig workers, and single inspection scheme are direct consequences.

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: Chandrayaan-3 landed near Moon's South Pole — India became:

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: An employer fails to deposit deducted employee share of EPF. Punishment is:

subject: Mixed Revision

explanation: XIII.53 Final Mock — GoI contributes 1.16% (capped). Combined with 8.33% employer = 9.49% of capped wages into Pension Fund.

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision

subject: Mixed Revision
stem: India's GST rate structure (2026) has slabs of:

subject: Mixed Revision

Inspections under S.13 Indian Geography Physical · Rivers · Economic · Census · Borders
